# Paper results tables

**Generated by `scripts/build_paper_tables.py` from the committed run records.** Do not
edit by hand: regenerate. Every number here is on the **test** split, from the single
frozen confirmatory execution of A1 step 10 (171 cells, 42 pairs, 0 failures).

Captions carry the limitation that applies to each table. A table lifted without its
caption is how a limitation gets lost.

*§6.3 requires mean gain ≥ 1.0 pp **and** a consistent sign across every paired
replicate. **No cell meets both.** Quote the Holm-adjusted p, not the raw one: six cells
were examined and the largest is reported. The baseline is the **frozen** order per cell,
not best-of-both, so the W8 rows carry an order uncertainty comparable to their effect.*

*Retention is `100 × dense_ppl / compressed_ppl`. The pruning and quantisation arms are

both prune 30%, and only the precision differs.*

| pythia-160m | 12 | 48 | 84,934,656 | 0.2997 | 8.0312 | 4.0312 |

*Mask sparsity sits just below 0.30 because the per-row prune count is an integer (B-46).
Effective bits exceed the nominal width by fp32 scale overhead. **Note the block counts:**
pythia-1b is *shallower* than pythia-410m, so the scale axis is confounded with depth
(F-38, limitations §2).*

## T7 — CPU deployment measurements

> ## ⚠️ DO NOT USE THIS TABLE FOR A LATENCY COMPARISON
>
> These are **incidental** measurements: each was taken inside its own cell, at whatever
> moment that cell happened to run, across six days of a grid that also saw commit
> exhaustion, process recycling and host standby. **They are not mutually comparable, and
> the `measured` column below shows why.**
>
> Worked example. pythia-1b dense reads 1041 ms and pythia-1b pruning 630 ms — an
> apparent **40% speedup from masking weights**. That is impossible: pruned weights stay
> FP32 and dense in storage, so the GEMM does identical work. The dense figure was
> measured on **2026-08-05** and all ten pruning figures on **2026-08-07**, where they are
> tightly consistent (627–650 ms). The gap is two days of machine state, not sparsity.
>
> **The authoritative latency result is [F-34](../docs/findings_log.md#f-34)**, a dedicated
> study under the §4.7 protocol — model-order rotation exists precisely to control the
> drift this table demonstrates. Cite F-34; use this table only to show coverage.

| Scale | Budget | Arm | Median latency (ms) | IQR | Runtime repr. | Measured |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pythia-160m | 30% + W8 | dense | 155.01 | 1.62 | fp32 | 2026-08-05 |
| pythia-160m | 30% + W8 | pruning | 153.88 | 2.74 | fp32 | 2026-08-05 |
| pythia-160m | 30% + W4 | pruning | 153.99 | 2.45 | fp32 | 2026-08-05 |
| pythia-410m | 30% + W8 | dense | 433.35 | 10.74 | fp32 | 2026-08-05 |
| pythia-410m | 30% + W8 | pruning | 427.38 | 3.97 | fp32 | 2026-08-06 |
| pythia-410m | 30% + W4 | pruning | 440.42 | 32.98 | fp32 | 2026-08-06 |
| pythia-1b | 30% + W8 | dense | 1041.36 | 32.39 | fp32 | 2026-08-05 |
| pythia-1b | 30% + W8 | pruning | 630.31 | 10.42 | fp32 | 2026-08-07 |
| pythia-1b | 30% + W4 | pruning | 639.36 | 22.80 | fp32 | 2026-08-07 |

*Replicate 0 only. **This is one sparsity (30%), not a curve** — RQ4's sparsity–speedup
relationship is unanswered (F-34, limitations §13).*

**Read which arms are missing.** Only the FP32 arms appear. Every packed arm —
quantisation, sequential and joint, at both W8 and W4 — is refused a latency by the
runtime-representation gate, because a packed artefact would be timed through a
dequantising path and the number would measure unpacking rather than inference. The
consequence is blunt and belongs in the text: **this study contains no joint-versus-
sequential latency comparison at all.** RQ4 is answerable only through the pruning-only
arm, whose weights stay FP32, and that arm shows no speedup from 30% unstructured
sparsity at any scale.*
